summary: Onslow County entry on the NC tower list; a 1938 state report, quoted by a lookout-history page, dates a 120-foot steel tower erected near Dixon to 1937.

events.note: 120-foot steel tower erected near Dixon by a CCC crew from Camp S-65. The source does not say which of the two Dixon entries it stood on.

evidence.supports: Dixon (new) on the North Carolina tower list: Onslow County, 34.61277, -77.48777
On February 13, 1937, one 120-foot steel tower was erected by the CCC near Dixon by a crew from Camp S-65
evidence.quote: February 13, 1937: One 120-foot steel tower was erected by the CCC near Dixon by a crew from Camp S-65.

notes_for_editor: The record has two Dixon entries (new and old) on the same list, a short distance apart. The only tower source found, a page quoting a 1938 state report, describes one 120-foot steel tower erected near Dixon in 1937 and does not say which entry it was. The naming hints the 1937 tower may be the old site, but no source says so; a human should check before tying the build to either entry. No fate, staffing or present-day source found. The Camp Lejeune base article on towers (lejeune.marines.mil) returned HTTP 403 and was not read; it may add detail.
